thought.text: The documented "temporary completion service" behavior needs emulation since systemd isn't really running. Let me apply the completion unit's actions and start the daemon.

reasoning_content:
The completion units are still present since systemd isn't actually running. According to the guide, after the web installer finishes, the path unit should trigger the complete service which enables the daemon and removes the temporary units. Since there's no real systemd, we need to emulate that to complete the documented behavior: enable/start daemon, disable & remove temporary completion units.

Let me run the completion service's ExecStart steps manually (that's what systemd would do). Run:
- systemctl enable --now qisutu-daemon.service (shim, will try to start via service which doesn't exist; we can start daemon manually)
- systemctl disable --now qisutu-install-complete.path
- rm the two files
- daemon-reload

And start the daemon manually as the qisutu user with the exact ExecStart command.

Let me do that. First check if QisutuConfig and DB connect work as qisutu user.

action.command:
systemctl disable --now qisutu-install-complete.path 2>&1
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.path /etc/systemd/system/qisutu-install-complete.service
systemctl daemon-reload
ls -la /etc/systemd/system/ | grep -i qisutu
echo "=== start daemon"
sudo -u qisutu QISUTU_HOME=/opt/qisutu /usr/bin/perl /opt/qisutu/bin/qisutu-daemon.pl --sleep 3 --max-jobs 100 > /tmp/daemon.log 2>&1 &
sleep 6
pgrep -af qisutu-daemon | head; echo "--- log"; tail -20 /tmp/daemon.log
